plants.habitat: Heathy and grassy open eucalypt forest and heathland. Very rarely seen. May occasionally be found where Pheladenia deformis and Caleana major occur. Curtis (1979) has recorded it from the north and north-east and it was also found on Schouten Is. in 1978.
plants.notes: A hybrid between Pheladenia deformis and Glossodia major. Both occur in fire-prone habitats and flower abundantly after fires. The hybrid is likely to be found in the first few years following a fire that stimulated flowering of the parent species. …

plants.name: Xanthorrhoea arenaria
plants.form: Trunkless, arising from a thick woody rootstock, with long, narrow leaves with sharp tips forming several crowns above ground.
plants.flowers: Distinctive flower spike, 7-40cm long.
plants.fruit: Capsule – turn from green to brown or black when ripe. Each capsule holds 2 matt black seeds, 8-12mm long.
plants.habitat: Sandy heaths, north-east and east coast from Bridport to Coles Bay.
plants.notes: Xanthorrhoea arenaria appears very similar to Xanthorrhoea bracteata; location is the best identifier. Susceptible to Phytophthora cinnamomi.

plants.name: Xanthorrhoea australis
plants.form: Perennial with an underground stem and a tall trunk densely covered with leaf bases.
plants.flowers: In a dense hard columnar spike up to 1.5m long, very numerous, small, white.
plants.fruit: Capsule – numerous, sharp-pointed; contained on spikes that turn from green to brown or black. Each capsule holds 2 seeds.
plants.habitat: Sandy soils in coastal or near-coastal areas, north-west, north-east, Furneaux Group and east coast.
plants.notes: Plants need a well-drained, sunny position. Leaf bases and trunk exude a strong smelling resin which has been used as a substitute for shellac. Resin is bee attracting. Flowers spring-summer or following fire. Foliage burns fiercely, leaving persistent crowded leaf bases.

plants.name: Xanthorrhoea bracteata
plants.form: Trunkless, arising from a thick woody rootstock, with long, narrow leaves with sharp tips forming several crowns above ground.
plants.flowers: Distinctive flower spike, 7.5-40cm long.
plants.fruit: Capsule – turn from green to brown or black when ripe. Each capsule holds 2 matt black seeds, 8-12mm long.
plants.habitat: Sandy soils, often acid and waterlogged. Coastal areas between the Asbestos Range and Waterhouse Point in the north-east.
plants.notes: Xanthorrhoea bracteata appears very similar to Xanthorrhoea arenari; location is the best identifier. Susceptible to Phytophthora cinnamomi.

plants.name: Xanthosia dissecta
plants.form: Small undershrub with a woody, short rootstock. Leaves usually hairless, alternate, and divided into 3 lobes, each of which is further divided into 3 or more segments.
plants.flowers: 2-7 flowers per umbel.
plants.habitat: Widespread and locally frequent in wet heaths.

plants.name: Xanthosia pilosa
plants.form: Small, softly hairy shrub with slender branches and alternate, 3-lobed leaves. Leaves dark green on the upper surface and white or yellow with brown hairs on the lower surface.
plants.flowers: Small, pale green to cream, in umbels.
plants.habitat: Widespread and frequent in heaths, sandy soils and open eucalypt forests.

plants.name: Xanthosia tasmanica
plants.form: Small, tufted plant with coarse, rigid hairs, a taproot and many slender, trailing branches. Leaves are alternate and up to 12mm long, and are hairy both sides.
plants.habitat: Occasional in sandy coastal heaths in the north, north-east and east.

plants.name: Xanthosia tridentata
plants.form: Small shrub with a short, erect stem, and 10-20cm long, slender spreading branches. Younger parts have scattered hairs.
plants.flowers: 1-3 flowers per umbel, with narrow, erect petals.
plants.habitat: Occasional in sandy coastal heaths in the east and north-east.

plants.name: Xerochrysum bicolor
plants.form: Annual or perennial herb with erect stem and slender woody tap-root.
plants.flowers: Flower heads solitary on the ends of main and side branches.
plants.habitat: Local, frequently in wet places near the coasts.

plants.name: Xerochrysum milliganii
plants.form: Perennial herb. Plants often form a dense patch of rosettes of bright green leaves.
plants.flowers: Single flower with yellow disc, on a woolly stem. Buds bright pink and brown on the outside.
plants.habitat: Western mountains, favouring high moorlands on nutrient-poor quartzite soils. Local in exposed places on mountain summits.
plants.notes: Plants do not live for many years in cultivation. Plants require moist soils rich in organic matter such as peat. Most plants develop a creeping rootstock in cultivation. They detest lack of moisture.

plants.name: Xerochrysum papillosum
plants.form: Stout annual or perennial herb with erect branched stem and tap-root.
plants.flowers: Heads 4-6.5cm in diameter with calyx bracts white, outer ones green/yellow with reddish tips.
plants.habitat: Coasts and islands in the eastern half of the State.
plants.notes: Develops a tap root. Must have unimpeded drainage.

plants.name: Xerochrysum subundulatum
plants.form: Perennial herb with branching underground stems forming large flat clumps.
plants.flowers: Large heads 3-4cm across, yellow disc florets with stiff bracts. Outer-brownish, inner-yellow.
plants.fruit: Achene – pappus with stiff yellow hairs.
plants.habitat: Widespread, alpine and sub-alpine grasslands, and heaths to mountain summits.
plants.notes: Adapts well to lower altitudes. Grows in most soils and full sun.

plants.name: Xyris marginata
plants.form: Perennial herb with numerous more or less erect and sometimes twisted leaves, forming small tussocks.
plants.flowers: Flowers with three round, golden yellow petals, each 8mm in diameter, with small, rounded teeth on the petal margins.
plants.habitat: Wet heaths on King Island, north-west, west coast, east coast and south-west, reaching 1070m altitude.
plants.notes: Useful for small rockeries and around ornamental pools.

plants.name: Xyris muelleri
plants.form: Tufted perennial herb with erect to spreading, often twisted leaves with pointed tips.
plants.flowers: Petals are pale yellow and 4-5mm wide.
plants.habitat: Wet heaths in the north-west, west coast, Central Highlands, south-west and Mt. Field, to 765m altitude.
plants.notes: Useful for small rockeries and around ornamental pools.

plants.name: Xyris operculata
plants.form: Herb with sub-terete leaves with sheathing base. Leaves may have a reddish/brown tint.
plants.flowers: Yellow flower – heads solitary on leafless stems. They open in succession 1 or 2 at a time.
plants.habitat: Wet, peaty heaths, sea level to alpine and sub-alpine.
plants.notes: Can be grown as a water feature provided the growing medium is changed regularly.

plants.name: Xyris tasmanica
plants.form: Slender perennial herb with rigid, thick, often twisted leaves with pointed tips, forming small tussocks.
plants.flowers: Round, pale to golden yellow petals, 5mm wide.
plants.fruit: Capsule – dehisces along the entire length.
plants.habitat: Wet heaths on King Island, north-west, north-east, west coast, east coast and south-west.
plants.notes: Useful for small rockeries and around ornamental pools.

plants.name: Zieria arborescens subsp. arborescens
plants.form: Tall shrub. Crushed leaves had a strong unpleasant smell.
plants.flowers: Each flower has 4 pink or white petals. They grow in clusters near the ends of branches.
plants.habitat: Common throughout the main island and on some Bass Strait Islands from sea level to about 1100 m. Usually found amongst the shrubby understorey of tall forest. Seems to do well after fires.
plants.notes: Moderate flammability. Resistant to Phytophthora cinnamomi.

plants.name: Zieria littoralis
plants.form: Much-branched shrub with highly aromatic foliage. Crushed leaves have a strong smell.
plants.flowers: Small cream or pale pink flowers with 4 petals; axillary, solitary or 2-3 together on short stalks.
plants.habitat: Occasional on the east coast.

plants.name: Zieria veronicea subsp. veronicea
plants.form: Small shrub
plants.flowers: Small white or pale pink flowers with 4 petals; axillary, solitary or 2-3 together on short stalks.
plants.habitat: Occasional on the east and north coasts.
plants.notes: Needs a well-drained site in half shade.

plants.name: Zostera muelleri subsp. muelleri
plants.form: Perennial seagrass with creeping rhizomes, forming extensive beds. Leaves ranging from 5-10cm in intertidal areas to 60cm long in estuaries.
plants.flowers: In spathes, large leaf-like structures enclosing the flowers, on fertile shoots.
plants.fruit: Fruit is firm; contains brown shining seeds, 2mm long.
plants.habitat: Intertidal, or permanently submerged in coastal creeks and estuaries on King Island, north-east, Furneaux Group and the east coast.
plants.notes: Sea grass

plants.name: Zoysia macrantha subsp. walshii
plants.form: Low-growing smooth perennial grass with well-developed rhizomes. Internodes short and purplish, and surrounded by shining, striped, straw-coloured scales.
plants.flowers: A short spike, up to 1.5cm long.
plants.habitat: Mostly coastal, especially on granite-derived sands, often just above the high-tide mark.
plants.notes: Commonly grazed by marsupials.
